pairs.why: A's black metal has soft, broad highlights close to the real cards' smooth satin finish, while B's red and black paint has sharper, lacquered specular spots.
Both rovers have the same smooth white satin plastic and soft rubber wheels, and the surface differences are too small to favour either one.
A's glass and ice have soft, broad highlights like the real glass, while B's bright caustic glow at the base and busier speckle look more rendered.
The real map is smooth, satin cream plastic with a clean edge, which B's smooth, moulded border matches better than A's crumpled paper folds.
A's canopy is smooth satin with soft highlights like the real one, while B adds crisp glossy edges and fussy rib hardware.
B's glossy dark keys on a matte body match the real calculator's material mix, while A's pale matte keys read as a different material.
B's slide is smooth satin plastic like the real one, while A adds chunky rivets, bolts and brighter gloss that the real card doesn't have.
B's orange rim has a soft glossy sheen and highlight like the real clock's rim, while A's rim looks flatter and more clay-like.
